theorem.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Let $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$
be $1$-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over
$(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.
If $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ and $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ are
representable by algebraic spaces and \'etale so is
$\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Etale permanence

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\overline{s}$ be a geometric point of $S$.
The category of \'etale neighborhoods is cofiltered. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(U_i, \overline{u}_i)_{i = 1, 2}$ be two \'etale neighborhoods of
$\overline{s}$ in $S$. Then there exists a third \'etale neighborhood
$(U, \overline{u})$ and morphisms
$(U, \overline{u}) \to (U_i, \overline{u}_i)$, $i = 1, 2$.
\item Let $h_1, h_2: (U, \overline{u}) \to (U', \overline{u}')$ be two
morphisms between \'etale neighborhoods of $\overline{s}$. Then there exist an
\'etale neighborhood $(U'', \overline{u}'')$ and a morphism
$h : (U'', \overline{u}'') \to (U, \overline{u})$
which equalizes $h_1$ and $h_2$, i.e., such that
$h_1 \circ h = h_2 \circ h$.
\end{enumerate}
Cofiltered means any pair of lifted étale neighbourhoods has a common *refinement*, and any two parallel morphisms are made equal after a further refinement. The fibre-product/étale diagonal construction uses the chosen geometric lifts.
hypotheses:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A **geometric point** $\bar s$ of a scheme $S$ is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. An **étale neighbourhood** of $\bar s$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ with $U\to S$ étale and a chosen $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $\bar s$; a morphism of such neighbourhoods is an $S$-morphism preserving the lifts. Their category is **cofiltered**, so a presheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** has stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar s}=\operatorname*{colim}_{(U,\bar u)}\mathcal F(U)$ over the opposite (filtered) category. Write $\mathcal F^\#$ for the associated sheaf. This is a *geometric* stalk, not merely a Zariski local-ring stalk.

theorem.title: Lemma — Hom from tensor product

conclusions: $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 6}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.
hypotheses: For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, the standing Cohen–Macaulay curve hypotheses imply $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional. Let $\omega_X$ be its coherent dualizing module, equal to $H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for the structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. A regular global section of an invertible sheaf is one whose multiplication map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is injective; an ample invertible sheaf is very ample if its global sections define a closed immersion into projective space.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ has a regular global section,
\item $H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$, and
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is ample.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 6}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Conormal effective Cartier divisor

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \mathrm{\acute etale}\}$. Consider the morphism
$$
\pi_S : (\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau \longrightarrow S_\tau
$$
of Topologies, Lemma \ref{topologies-lemma-at-the-bottom} or
\ref{topologies-lemma-at-the-bottom-etale}. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on
$S_\tau$. Then $\pi_S^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ is given by the rule
$$
(\pi_S^{-1}\mathcal{F})(T) = \Gamma(T_\tau, f_{small}^{-1}\mathcal{F})
$$
where $f : T \to S$. Moreover, $\pi_S^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the
sheaf condition with respect to fpqc coverings.
For τ=Zariski or étale, the site morphism π_S is from the **big to small** τ-site; the inverse-image sheaf on a big-site object T is computed by *global sections of a small-site inverse-image sheaf on T*. The resulting presheaf satisfies even **fpqc descent**, a condition stronger than τ-sheafhood.

A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

An **fpqc cover** means a flat jointly surjective family with the finite affine-source cover condition over each affine open.

theorem.title: Lemma — Describe pullback

conclusions:
$f = s/s'$
is an element of $R(X)^*$ and we have
$$
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s)[Z]
=

$$

hypotheses:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s, s' \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be nonzero
meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{L}$.
theorem.statement:
For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s, s' \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be nonzero
meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{L}$. Then $f = s/s'$
is an element of $R(X)^*$ and we have
$$
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s)[Z]
=
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s')[Z]
+
\text{div}(f)
$$
as Weil divisors.

theorem.title: Lemma — Finite residue extension closed

conclusions: There exists i\ge 0 such that f_i:X_i\to Y_i is affine.
hypotheses: I is a directed indexing set, 0\in I, and (S_i)_{i\in I} is an inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms.
S=\varprojlim_{i\in I}S_i.
f_0:X_0\to Y_0 is a morphism of schemes over S_0.
S_0, X_0, Y_0 are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
For every i\ge 0, f_i:X_i\to Y_i is obtained from f_0 by base change along S_i\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is the corresponding base change of f_0 along S\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is affine.
theorem.statement: Let \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) be a directed inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit \(S=\varprojlim_i S_i\). Fix \(0\in I\) and a morphism of \(S_0\)-schemes \(f_0:X_0\to Y_0\) with \(S_0,X_0,Y_0\) quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each \(i\ge 0\), let \(f_i:X_i\to Y_i\) be the base change of \(f_0\) to \(S_i\), and let \(f:X\to Y\) be its base change to \(S\). If \(f\) is affine, then there exists \(i\ge 0\) such that \(f_i\) is affine.

theorem.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Let $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$, and assume the Noetherian local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is Cohen–Macaulay (its depth equals its Krull dimension). Suppose for every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $X$ containing $x$, the residue extension satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(\xi))}\kappa(\xi)\le r$ for some integer $r\ge0$. Then $H^i(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x\ne0$ implies $i\ge-r$. Moreover the finitely generated $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x$ satisfies Serre's condition $(S_2)$: for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, its localization has depth at least $\min\{2,\dim\operatorname{Supp}(H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x)_{\mathfrak p}\}$, with the usual convention for zero modules.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

theorem.title: Lemma — Flat over thickening

conclusions:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ which
is regular. Let $x \in X$ be a closed point and denote $\mathcal{O}_x$
the skyscraper sheaf at $x$ with value $\kappa(x)$. Let $K$ in
$D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\Ext^i_X(\mathcal{O}_x, K) = 0$ then there exists an open
neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $H^{i - d_x}(K)|_U = 0$ where
$d_x = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item If $\Hom_X(\mathcal{O}_x, K[i]) = 0$ for all
$i \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $K$ is zero in an open neighbourhood of $x$.
\item If $\Ext^i_X(K, \mathcal{O}_x) = 0$ then there exists an open
neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $H^i(K^\vee)|_U = 0$.
\item If $\Hom_X(K, \mathcal{O}_x[i]) = 0$ for all
$i \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $K$ is zero in an open neighbourhood of $x$.
\item If $H^i(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_x) = 0$
then there exists an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that
$H^i(K)|_U = 0$.
\item If $H^i(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_x) = 0$
for $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K$ is zero in an
open neighbourhood of $x$.
\end{enumerate}
Each clause has its own vanishing hypothesis: individual Ext^i gives a single nearby cohomology sheaf vanishing, while all shifts give complete vanishing near x; the two Hom directions correspond to K and K^vee respectively.

theorem.title: Lemma — Bourbaki finite type general base at point

conclusions:
Let $(R, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local ring. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is henselian,
\item for any $f\in R[T]$ and any factorization $\bar f = g_0 h_0$ in
$\kappa[T]$ with $\gcd(g_0, h_0)=1$, there exists a factorization $f = gh$ in
$R[T]$ with $\bar g = g_0$ and $\bar h = h_0$,
\item any finite $R$-algebra $S$ is isomorphic to a finite product of
local rings finite over $R$,
\item any finite type $R$-algebra $A$ is isomorphic to a product
$A \cong A' \times C$ where $A' \cong A_1 \times \ldots \times A_r$
is a product of finite local $R$-algebras and all the irreducible
components of $C \otimes_R \kappa$ have dimension at least 1,
\item if $A$ is an \'etale $R$-algebra and $\mathfrak n$ is a maximal ideal of
$A$ lying over $\mathfrak m$ such that $\kappa \cong A/\mathfrak n$, then there
exists an isomorphism $\varphi : A \cong R \times A'$ such that
$\varphi(\mathfrak n) = \mathfrak m \times A' \subset R \times A'$.
\end{enumerate}
All five equivalent conditions apply to the **same arbitrary local ring** (not necessarily Noetherian). The finite algebra condition includes decomposition into *local* finite R-algebras; the condition for étale A includes a specified maximal ideal n over m with κ≅A/n. The polynomial factorization hypothesis is exactly as stated in source, including coprimality in κ[T].

theorem.title: Lemma — Eventually separated

conclusions: The Hodge-level Gysin maps induced by local cohomology commute with exterior differentiation.
hypotheses: $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a Koszul-regular finitely presented closed immersion of codimension $c$.
theorem.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.
Assume further that $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Koszul regular. Then $\mathcal H^j_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})=0$ for $j<c$, and the local-cohomology Gysin morphism induces maps
$$\gamma^{p,q}:H^q(Z,\Omega^p_{Z/S})\longrightarrow H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}).$$
These are compatible with the maps induced by the de Rham differential: for each $p,q$, $d\circ\gamma^{p,q}=\gamma^{p+1,q}\circ d$ (the target in the first composite has differential form degree $p+c+1$).

hypotheses: Let $i : Z \to X$ be a Koszul regular closed immersion.
theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a Koszul regular closed immersion.
Then there exists a surjective smooth morphism $X' \to X$ such
that the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$ of $i$ is
a regular immersion.

hypotheses: X scheme, E perfect.
U⊂X SCHEME THEORETICALLY DENSE OPEN with every H^i(E|U) finite locally free constant rank r_i.
theorem.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ be perfect.
Let $U \subset X$ be a scheme theoretically dense open subscheme
such that $H^i(E|_U)$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r_i$

$H^i(Lb^*E)$ is a perfect $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module
of tor dimension $\leq 1$ for all $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Left dual derived

conclusions: For any left multiplicative system $S$, the localization has cokernels preserved by $Q$.

hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category.
theorem.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $S$ is a left multiplicative system, then
the category $S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ has cokernels and the functor
$Q : \mathcal{A} \to S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ commutes with them.
\item If $S$ is a right multiplicative system, then
the category $S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ has kernels and the functor
$Q : \mathcal{A} \to S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ commutes with them.
\item If $S$ is a multiplicative system, then the category
$S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ is abelian and the functor
$Q : \mathcal{A} \to S^{-1}\mathcal{A}$ is exact.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: The following conditions are equivalent: $R$ is a normal ring, ; $R$ is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions, and ; $R$ is a finite product of normal domains.

theorem.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Assume $R$ is reduced and has finitely many
minimal primes. Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is a normal ring,
\item $R$ is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions, and
\item $R$ is a finite product of normal domains.
\end{enumerate}
A normal domain means a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. A normal ring means a ring whose localization at every prime ideal is a normal domain.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.
theorem.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. Assume $p$ is representable
by algebraic spaces and an open immersion. Then $p$ is limit preserving

theorem.statement:

\item The support of $\sigma$ is closed in $U$.
\item The support of $\sigma + \sigma'$ is contained in the union of

abelian sheaves on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$, then the support of $\varphi(\sigma)$

supports of all local sections of $\mathcal{F}$.

of $\mathcal{G}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{F}$.

of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Proposition — Enough acyclics

conclusions:
Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ is syntomic and induces a surjective map on spectra, or
\item $A \to B$ is a faithfully flat local complete intersection, or
\item $A \to B$ is faithfully flat of finite type with Gorenstein fibres.
\end{enumerate}
Then $K \in D(A)$ is a dualizing complex for $A$ if and only if
$K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B$ is a dualizing complex for $B$.
Syntomic means flat, finitely presented and locally complete intersection. The three alternatives all include faithful flatness and ensure that the relative shriek complex is invertible; ascension and descension are separate implications.

A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

conclusions: Unique pro extension of morphisms, existence of systems, and uniqueness up to pro-isomorphism.
hypotheses: Noetherian open immersion, Deligne systems, bounded coherent derived restrictions.
theorem.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of Noetherian schemes: (1) if $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ are Deligne systems with constant restriction values $K,L$ on $U$, any morphism $\alpha:K\to L$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ extends to a **unique morphism of pro-objects** $(K_n)\to(L_n)$ that restricts to $\alpha$ (not necessarily a levelwise map with matching indices); (2) every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ occurs as the common restriction value of some Deligne system on $X$; and (3) such a pro-object is unique up to the unique pro-isomorphism inducing the identity on $K$. Thus $K\mapsto(K_n)$ defines the coherent pro-extension functor $Rj_!$.

conclusions: The inverse system $M_n=H^p(\mathcal C,\mathcal F_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition (indeed eventual stable images admit a uniform shift as in the source footnote).

theorem.statement:
An inverse system $(M_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition when, for every fixed $n$, the images of the transition maps $M_m\to M_n$ stabilize for all sufficiently large $m$. The graded ring $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ is the associated graded ring of the $I$-adic filtration. For a site $\mathcal C$ and ring $A$ with ideal $I$, an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules $\cdots\to\mathcal F_3\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_1$ is assumed to have $\mathcal F_n\cong\mathcal F_{n+1}/I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$. The graded module is built from **degree $p+1$** cohomology of the submodules $I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$.

Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules on $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Assume
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
$$
satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module.
Then the inverse system $M_n = H^p(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition\footnote{In fact, there exists
a $c \geq 0$ such that $\Im(M_n \to M_{n - c})$ is the stable image

theorem.title: Lemma — Quasi excellent nagata

conclusions: Depth agrees with first nonzero Ext and local cohomology, with Ext-vanishing below depth.
hypotheses: A Noetherian, I ideal, M finite and IM≠M; N finite I-power torsion for last part.
theorem.statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$, ideal $I$ and finitely generated $A$-module $M$, define $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ to be the maximal length of an $M$-regular sequence of elements of $I$ (and $\infty$ by convention if $IM=M$). A sequence $(x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ is $M$-regular if each $x_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})M$ and the final quotient is nonzero. Assume $IM\ne M$, so $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ is finite. Then the following three integers are equal:
\[
\operatorname{depth}_I(M)
=\min\{i\ge0:\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(A/I,M)\ne0\}
=\min\{i\ge0:H_I^i(M)\ne0\},
\]
where $H_I^i(M)$ is the cohomology of the derived $I$-power-torsion functor (equivalently Čech local cohomology since $A$ is Noetherian). Moreover if $N$ is any finite module with $I^nN=0$ for some $n$, then $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(N,M)=0$ for every $i<\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$.

Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $Z \to X$ be an immersion.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation,
\item $Z \to X$ is a relative quasi-regular immersion.
\end{enumerate}
Then $Z \to X$ is a regular immersion and
the same remains true after any base change.

theorem.title: Lemma — Finite locally free

conclusions: a_f preserves arbitrary direct sums.

theorem.statement: Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. For every family $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ of objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the canonical map $\bigoplus_\lambda a_f(K_\lambda)\to a_f(\bigoplus_\lambda K_\lambda)$ is an isomorphism. Thus the right adjoint to the derived pushforward preserves arbitrary coproducts, not merely finite sums.

theorem.title: Proposition — Polynomial

conclusions: If there are integral effective Cartier divisors $D_i\subset X$ and a closed subset $Z^{\prime}\subset X$ whose irreducible components have codimension at least2 such that $Z\subset Z^{\prime}\cup\bigcup_iD_i$ set-theoretically, then there exist nonnegative integers $a_i$, zero for almost all $i$, such that $D=\sum_i a_iD_i$ is contained in $Z$ as a closed subscheme and $D\to Z$ is an isomorphism on an open $U\subset Z$ whose complement has all irreducible components of codimension at least2 in $X$.
If $Z$ is nowhere dense and either every $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for $x\in Z$ is a UFD or $X$ is regular, then such a family $D_i$ and subset $Z^{\prime}$ exist.
hypotheses: $X$ is a Noetherian scheme and $Z\subset X$ a closed subscheme.
theorem.statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Assume there exist
\begin{enumerate}
\item a collection of integral effective Cartier divisors
$D_i \subset X$, $i \in I$
\item a closed subset $Z' \subset X$ all of whose irreducible components
have codimension $\geq 2$ in $X$

\end{enumerate}
such that $Z \subset Z' \cup \bigcup_{i \in I} D_i$ set-theoretically.
Then there exist integers $a_i \geq 0$ with $a_i = 0$ for almost all $i \in I$
such that the effective Cartier divisor
$$
D = \sum a_i D_i
$$
is contained in $Z$ and such that the inclusion morphism $D \to Z$
is an isomorphism away from codimension $2$ in $X$
(in the sense that there exists an open $U \subset Z$ such that
$D \cap U \to Z \cap U$ is an isomorphism and such that every
irreducible component of $Z \setminus U$ has codimension $\geq 2$ in $X$).
When $Z$ is nowhere dense in $X$ existence of the $D_i$, $i \in I$ and $Z'$
is guaranteed if $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a UFD for all $x \in Z$
or if $X$ is regular.

theorem.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_T W]_{q+r}$ with scheme-theoretic multiplicities. It also induces a map on Chow groups.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Assume $X$, $Y$
are integral and $n = \dim_\delta(Y)$.

$$
f^*(c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [Y]) = c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \cap [X]
$$
in $\mathrm{CH}_{n + r - 1}(X)$.

\begin{enumerate}

$$
is a presheaf. And the colimit is a directed one.

theorem.title: Lemma — Base change by space representable by space

conclusions: Triangle can be represented by a compatible inverse system of Deligne triangles on X.
hypotheses: Noetherian j:U→X, a bounded-coherent distinguished triangle on U.
theorem.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Suppose $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ is a distinguished triangle in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$. Then there exists an inverse system of distinguished triangles $K_n\to L_n\to M_n\to K_n[1]$ in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ such that each of the three inverse systems is a Deligne system and the restriction of every displayed triangle to $U$ is isomorphic to the original triangle. This is a *systemwise existence* statement for representing exact triangles, not strict exactness of a naive functor to an abelian category.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

theorem.statement:
On a site C, an object U is **weakly contractible** if every epimorphism of sheaves of sets F→G induces a surjection on sections F(U)→G(U). This is stronger than topological weak contractibility of a space. For a ringed site (C,O), extension by zero j_{U!}O_U is the left adjoint to localization/restriction at U. Let B⊂Ob(C) consist of weakly contractible objects such that **every** site object admits a covering by members of B. The assertion is a seven-part conjunction, including exactness, truncation completeness, derived products and inverse-limit formulas. The tower/derived-limit results use **countable sequential** inverse systems, with R^1lim described by the difference map on products.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
such that every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ is weakly contractible and
every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering by elements of $\mathcal{B}$.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item A complex $\mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3$
of $\mathcal{O}$-modules is exact, if and only if
$\mathcal{F}_1(U) \to \mathcal{F}_2(U) \to \mathcal{F}_3(U)$
is exact for all $U \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item Every object $K$ of $D(\mathcal{O})$ is a derived limit
of its canonical truncations: $K = R\lim \tau_{\geq -n} K$.
\item Given an inverse system
$\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1$
with surjective transition maps, the projection
$\lim \mathcal{F}_n \to \mathcal{F}_1$ is surjective.
\item Products are exact on $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$.
\item Products on $D(\mathcal{O})$ can be computed by taking
products of any representative complexes.
\item If $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ is an inverse system of $\mathcal{O}$-modules,
then $R^p\lim \mathcal{F}_n = 0$ for all $p > 1$ and
$$
R^1\lim \mathcal{F}_n  =
\Coker(\prod \mathcal{F}_n \to \prod \mathcal{F}_n)
$$
where the map is $(x_n) \mapsto (x_n - f(x_{n + 1}))$.
\item If $(K_n)$ is an inverse system of objects of $D(\mathcal{O})$,
then there are short exact sequences
$$
0 \to R^1\lim H^{p - 1}(K_n) \to H^p(R\lim K_n) \to
\lim H^p(K_n) \to 0
$$
\end{enumerate}

theorem.statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. For any $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the canonical morphism on global derived Hom complexes
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K),
\]
induced by $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_X(E,a_f(K))\to R\mathcal Hom_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ and derived global sections, is a quasi-isomorphism (hence an isomorphism in the derived category of abelian groups). This is stronger than merely the degree-zero Hom-set adjunction but does *not* imply that the underlying sheaf-level map is an isomorphism before quasi-coherating.

The following conditions are equivalent: The domain $R$ is a normal domain, ; for every prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$ the local ring

hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain.
theorem.statement:
Let $R$ be a domain. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The domain $R$ is a normal domain,
\item for every prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$ the local ring
$R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain, and
\item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ the ring $R_{\mathfrak m}$
is a normal domain.
\end{enumerate}
A normal domain means a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. A normal ring means a ring whose localization at every prime ideal is a normal domain.

theorem.title: Lemma — Base change finite presentation

conclusions: $c^*\omega_Y \cong \omega_X$.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *stable curve* (in the situation $g\ge2$) has no rational tails or rational bridges, equivalently each genus-zero irreducible component meets the remainder of $X$ in at least three geometric points. Its dualizing sheaf $\omega_X$ is invertible. A contraction to a stable curve means a proper morphism $c:X\to X_{\mathrm{st}}$ obtained by successively contracting rational tails and bridges and whose target has no such components.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $c : X \to Y$ be a morphism of proper schemes over $k$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{O}_Y = c_*\mathcal{O}_X$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal{O}_X = 0$,
\item $X$ and $Y$ are reduced, Gorenstein, and have dimension $1$,

conclusions:

\item $R^h$ is henselian, $R^{sh}$ is strictly henselian,
\item $\mathfrak m R^h$ (resp.\ $\mathfrak m R^{sh}$) is the
maximal ideal of $R^h$ (resp.\ $R^{sh}$), and

conclusions: The diagonal multiplication-kernel annihilator is generated by the image of det(gij).

theorem.statement: Let $A\to P$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in P$ be a *Koszul-regular sequence* (its Koszul complex is exact in positive degrees). Assume $B=P/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ is flat over $A$. Suppose $g_1,\ldots,g_n\in P\otimes_AB$ form a Koszul-regular sequence and generate the kernel of the natural multiplication map $P\otimes_AB\to B$. Choose elements $g_{ij}\in P\otimes_AB$ such that $f_i\otimes1=\sum_{j=1}^n g_{ij}g_j$. Let $\bar\delta\in B\otimes_AB$ be the image of $\det(g_{ij})$ under the map $P\otimes_AB\to B\otimes_AB$. Then the annihilator ideal $J=\operatorname{Ann}_{B\otimes_AB}(\ker(B\otimes_AB\xrightarrow\mu B))$ is the principal ideal $(\bar\delta)$ of $B\otimes_AB$.

hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Countable fg tensor

conclusions: The canonical mate Rg'_*a'→a Rg_* is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Cartesian qcqs square, g flat or f and g Tor independent, and right adjoints as defined.
theorem.statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{matrix}
\]
where $f$ and $g$ are *Tor-independent*, meaning the higher Tor sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{Y'}$ over $\mathcal O_Y$ vanish. Write $a=a_f$ and $a'=a_{f'}$ for the respective right adjoints of derived pushforward. The usual derived base-change map is $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*L(g')^*$; under Tor-independence it is an isomorphism. Its adjoint mate is the isomorphism $\xi:Rg'_*a'\xrightarrow{\sim} a Rg_*$. The duality base-change map is the natural transformation $\alpha:L(g')^*a\to a' Lg^*$ obtained by composing unit $\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^*$, $\xi^{-1}$, and counit $L(g')^*Rg'_*\to\mathrm{id}$. Then the canonical adjoint-mate transformation $\xi:Rg'_*a'\to a\,Rg_*$, considered as a natural transformation from $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y'})$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, is an isomorphism. This holds if $g$ is flat, and more generally whenever $f$ and $g$ are Tor-independent; the square need not be proper.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

Let $X$, $Y$ be locally of finite type over $S$.

$U \subset Y$ such that $f|_{f^{-1}(U)} : f^{-1}(U) \to U$

theorem.title: Lemma — Product representable by spaces

conclusions: Derived local cohomology and derived completion are quasi-inverse between torsion and complete subcategories.
hypotheses: A arbitrary, I finitely generated, derived torsion and completion via augmented Čech.
theorem.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Define the *derived $I$-adic completion* of $K\in D(A)$ by $K^\wedge=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r),K)$, with its natural unit $K\to K^\wedge$. Let $D_{\rm comp}(A,I)$ be the full subcategory of derived $I$-complete complexes, i.e. those for which this unit is an isomorphism (equivalently $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_{f_i},K)=0$ for all $i$). These definitions use the derived Čech model and do not assume $A$ Noetherian or identify derived completion automatically with the naive inverse limit for arbitrary $K$. Then the restrictions
\[
R\Gamma_Z:D_{\rm comp}(A,I)\longrightarrow D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(-)^\wedge:D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\longrightarrow D_{\rm comp}(A,I)
\]
are quasi-inverse exact equivalences of triangulated categories. More precisely $R\Gamma_Z(K^\wedge)\simeq R\Gamma_Z(K)$ and $(R\Gamma_ZK)^\wedge\simeq K^\wedge$ for any $K\in D(A)$. This is the derived torsion-completion equivalence, not classical equality of torsion and complete modules.

be the normalization. Let $x \in X$ denote a closed point. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ is finite, surjective, and birational,
\item $\mathcal{O}_X \subset \nu_*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu}$ and
$\nu_*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu}/\mathcal{O}_X$ is a direct sum of
skyscraper sheaves with value $\mathcal{Q}_x$ at $x$ which is nonzero
if and only if $x$ is a singular point of $X$,
\item $A' = (\nu_*\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu})_x$ is the integral closure
of $A = \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ in its total ring of fractions,
\item $\mathcal{Q}_x = A'/A$ has finite length equal to the
$\delta$-invariant of $X$ at $x$,
\item $A'$ is a semi-local ring which is a finite product of
Dedekind domains,
\item $A^\wedge$ is a reduced Noetherian complete
local ring of dimension $1$,
\item $(A')^\wedge$ is the integral closure of $A^\wedge$
in its total ring of fractions,
\item $(A')^\wedge$ is a finite product of
complete discrete valuation rings, and
\item $A'/A \cong (A')^\wedge/A^\wedge$.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Genus normalization

conclusions: Relative perfectness and derived self-duality of the upper-shriek structure complex.
hypotheses: f flat in FTS_S.
theorem.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ is flat. An object $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is *$Y$-perfect* if it is pseudo-coherent and has locally bounded Tor-amplitude relative to $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$. Then $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is $Y$-perfect and the homothety map
\[
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(f^!\mathcal O_Y,f^!\mathcal O_Y)
\]
is an isomorphism. Flatness here is part of a finite-type morphism in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$.

theorem.title: Lemma — What gets inverted

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

theorem.statement:
A Noetherian local ring $A$ is *Gorenstein* if $A[0]$ is a dualizing complex (equivalently its self-injective dimension is finite). A general Noetherian ring is Gorenstein when all local rings are. An object of the derived category is *invertible* if it admits a two-sided derived-tensor inverse; locally it is a shift of a rank-one projective module. A *local complete intersection* map is locally a quotient of a polynomial algebra by a Koszul-regular sequence.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A$ has a dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is Gorenstein $\Leftrightarrow$ $\omega_A^\bullet$ is an invertible
object of $D(A)$,
\item $A_\mathfrak p$ is Gorenstein $\Leftrightarrow$
$(\omega_A^\bullet)_\mathfrak p$ is an invertible object of
$D(A_\mathfrak p)$,
\item $\{\mathfrak p \in \Spec(A) \mid A_\mathfrak p\text{ is Gorenstein}\}$
is an open subset.
\end{enumerate}
\item If $A$ is Gorenstein, then $A$ has a dualizing complex if and
only if $A[0]$ is a dualizing complex.
\end{enumerate}

A derived-invertible object is locally a shift of an invertible module, not necessarily a module in degree zero.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, m∈Z, and K,L∈D(O).
theorem.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O) and integer m, a complex E^bullet is **m-pseudo-coherent** if locally on every site object it admits a map from a strictly perfect complex inducing isomorphisms in H^j for j>m and a **surjection** in H^m. An object E∈D(O) is m-pseudo-coherent if any representing complex has this property (equivalently some representative; see source lines 12038–12057). Pseudo-coherent means m-pseudo-coherent for every integer m, and it does **not** imply global bounded-above without extra quasi-compactness. Being a direct summand is stated for two objects K,L with their sum K⊕L in the derived category; the two variants m-pseudo-coherence and full pseudo-coherence are separate but analogous.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $m \in \mathbf{Z}$.
If $K \oplus L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent (resp.\ pseudo-coherent)
in $D(\mathcal{O})$ so are $K$ and $L$.

conclusions: Any left exact or right exact $F$ is additive.
$F$ is left exact iff it carries each short exact sequence to a left-exact sequence beginning at zero.

$0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$

is exact.

theorem.title: Lemma — Exact functor

conclusions: A unique isomorphism respecting all local normalizing identifications exists.
hypotheses: Finite-type T/S, fixed base dualizing D_S, fixed separated finite open cover U and normalized pairs including α_i.
theorem.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. If two normalized pairs $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ and $(D'_T,\{\alpha'_i\})$ exist for the *same* base complex $D_S$ and covering $\mathcal U$, then there exists a **unique** isomorphism $u:D_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D'_T$ in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ such that $\alpha'_i\circ u|_{U_i}=\alpha_i$ for every $i$. The uniqueness is relative to the specified normalizing isomorphisms, not a claim that the underlying dualizing complex has no automorphisms.

theorem.title: Lemma — Descending property integral

conclusions: Relative cup/evaluation/trace gives perfect field pairings for every cohomological degree.
hypotheses: X proper/k, D_X right-adjoint dualizing, E perfect, trace t.
theorem.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a proper finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension $d$. Let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $a_p$ be the right adjoint to $Rp_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, where $Rp_*$ identifies with derived global sections $R\Gamma(X,-)$. Define the *canonical normalized dualizing complex* $D_X=a_p(k[0])$; it is the compactification-based $p^!k$. Put $\omega_X=H^{-d}(D_X)$ and let $t:H^0(X,D_X)\to k$ be the cohomological trace induced by the adjunction counit $R\Gamma(X,D_X)\to k$. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be a perfect complex, with derived dual $E^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(E,\mathcal O_X)$ and evaluation $\epsilon:E^\vee\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}E\to\mathcal O_X$. For each $i\in\mathbf Z$, the cup product, then evaluation, then trace $t$ defines a bilinear pairing
\[
H^i(X,D_X\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}E^\vee)\times H^{-i}(X,E)\to k.
\]
Each pairing is *perfect*: the two cohomology groups are finite-dimensional over $k$ and identify with each other's linear duals. The claim uses perfectness of $E$ and properness of $X$ and does not extend blindly to arbitrary unbounded quasi-coherent $E$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Compose base change

conclusions: The finite-syntomic de Rham trace exists, extends the algebra trace, satisfies the projection formula, and descends to relative de Rham complexes over any common base $S$.
hypotheses: $f:Y\to X$ is finite syntomic (and, for the final assertion, is over $S$).
theorem.statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite syntomic morphism of schemes. There is a canonical trace morphism of absolute algebraic de Rham complexes
$$\Theta_{Y/X}:f_*\Omega^\bullet_{Y/\mathbf Z}\longrightarrow\Omega^\bullet_{X/\mathbf Z}$$
whose component in degree $0$ is the usual algebra trace $\operatorname{Tr}_f:f_*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$, and which satisfies the projection formula
$$\Theta_{Y/X}(f^*\omega\wedge\eta)=\omega\wedge\Theta_{Y/X}(\eta)$$
for local forms $\omega$ on $X$ and $\eta$ on $Y$. If $f$ is a morphism over a scheme $S$, this descends to a morphism of relative de Rham complexes
$$f_*\Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}\longrightarrow\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}.$$

theorem.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
The full subcategory $\text{Ac}$ of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$
consisting of acyclic modules is a strictly full saturated triangulated
subcategory of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$.
The corresponding saturated multiplicative system

of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$ is the class $\text{Qis}$
of quasi-isomorphisms. In particular, the kernel of the localization
functor
$$
Q : K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}) \to
\text{Qis}^{-1}K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})
$$
is $\text{Ac}$. Moreover, the functor $H^0$ factors through $Q$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Lift through quasi isomorphism

conclusions:
Let $A\to B$ be finite type ring map and $\mathfrak p \subset A$ a prime
ideal. Then there exist an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ and a prime
$\mathfrak p' \subset A'$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\kappa(\mathfrak p) = \kappa(\mathfrak p')$,
\item
$ B \otimes_A A' = B_1\times \ldots \times B_r \times C$,
\item
$ A'\to B_i$ is finite and there exists a unique prime $q_i\subset B_i$ lying
over $\mathfrak p'$, and
\item all irreducible components of the fibre
$\Spec(C \otimes_{A'} \kappa(\mathfrak p'))$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak p'$
have dimension at least 1.
\end{enumerate}
The étale extension A→A' includes a **chosen prime p' above p with identical residue field**, and the decomposition B⊗_A A'=∏B_i×C is global over A'. Each finite B_i has exactly one prime over p'; C has **no zero-dimensional irreducible component in the fibre** at p', though it can have positive-dimensional fibre components.

Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

theorem.title: Theorem — Quasi finite etale locally

conclusions: The triangle K→L→M→K[1] whose boundary is represented by π·d_L·s for graded splittings π,s is, up to canonical isomorphism in the homotopy category, independent of the splittings.
hypotheses: (A,d) is a dg algebra and 0→K→L→M→0 is an admissible short exact sequence of dg A-modules.
theorem.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let
$0 \to K \to L \to M \to 0$ be an admissible short exact sequence
of differential graded $A$-modules. The triangle
\begin{equation}
K \to L \to M \xrightarrow{\delta} K[1]
\end{equation}
where $\delta$ is the connecting arrow represented by $\pi\circ\mathrm d_L\circ s:M\to K[1]$ for graded $A$-module splittings $s:M\to L$ and $\pi:L\to K$ with $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}s$ is, up to canonical
isomorphism in $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$, independent of the choices of such graded splittings.

theorem.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\Sch_\etale$ be a big \'etale
site containing $S$.
The functor
$(\textit{Aff}/S)_\etale \to (\Sch/S)_\etale$
is special cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi from

theorem.title: Lemma — Normalization and henselization

conclusions: An exact triangulated functor $Lf^*:D(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O)$ exists, and for any K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O'$-modules having flat terms, $Lf^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ is represented by the ordinary termwise pullback $f^*\mathcal K^\bullet$.

hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')$ is a morphism of ringed topoi.

A complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules is K-flat when $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ (sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). For an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')$, $f^*$ is the ordinary module pullback $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O')\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. The source names the result `derived-base-change` but the claim is the **existence and computation of derived pullback** (not a cartesian base-change isomorphism).

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. There exists an exact functor
$$
Lf^* : D(\mathcal{O}') \longrightarrow D(\mathcal{O})
$$
of triangulated categories so that
$Lf^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet = f^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ for any
K-flat complex $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ with flat terms and
in particular for any bounded above complex of flat $\mathcal{O}'$-modules.

theorem.title: Lemma — Characterize integral

conclusions:
$\mathcal{J}$ is regular
(resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) if and only if

theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{J}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
Then $\mathcal{J}$ is regular
(resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) if and only if
for every $x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J})$ there exists
an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$, $U = \Spec(A)$
such that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and such that $I$

quasi-regular) sequence $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in A$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Dualizing localize

conclusions: Base change of the projection comparison is compatible with α (commutative square).
hypotheses: Cartesian Tor-independent qcqs square, canonical α and projection comparisons μ.
theorem.statement:
For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for the unbounded derived category of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology on $T$, and let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$. Its unit and counit are $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_fRf_*$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes $X'=X\times_Y Y'\xrightarrow{g'}X$ above $g:Y'\to Y$ and with vertical maps $f':X'\to Y'$ and $f:X\to Y$. Assume the pair $(f,g)$ is Tor-independent, so that the standard derived base-change map $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*L(g')^*$ is an isomorphism. Let $a_f,a_{f'}$ be the respective right adjoints. The *duality base-change transformation* is $\alpha:L(g')^*a_f\to a_{f'}Lg^*$, constructed by adjunction from $\beta$ using its mate $Rg'_*a_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_fRg_*$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. Then for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the square
\[
\begin{matrix}
L(g')^*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))&\xrightarrow{L(g')^*(\mu_{f,K})}&L(g')^*a_f(K)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\alpha_K\\
L(f')^*Lg^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_{f'}(\mathcal O_{Y'})&\xrightarrow{\mu_{f',Lg^*K}}&a_{f'}(Lg^*K)
\end{matrix}
\]
commutes, where the left vertical map uses derived-pullback associativity and $\alpha_{\mathcal O_Y}:L(g')^*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_{f'}(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. All tensors in each row are over the relevant source scheme.

theorem.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$.
